description:
Advances: ancora.tasks

Stage: L10 (05a-stages-library.md). Plan run dir on epic ancora-yzu.

Deliverable:
mix spec.prime (--base, --since, --root, --spec-dir; no --json), mix spec.next (--base, --since, --verbose; classification and reconciliation labels carried verbatim from specled_ex), mix spec.status (--root, --spec-dir; exit 0 always; derived-set report derived subjects=<N> empty=<E> thin(<3)=<T> plus per-subject rows with generated=<project>+<dep> split and an acknowledged label for subjects carrying an override; thin=3 documented constant, non-configurable). No verdict lines on any of the three; error paths through gated (bad base = env-style message, exit 1). prime --base HEAD prints the loop ending with the check command and read_protocol/0.

Verification:
- Tests to pass: tagged_tests covering ancora.tasks.report_task_flags, next_labels_verbatim, status_derived_report, prime_loop
- Behaviors to demonstrate: ancora.tasks.scenario.json_rejected_on_reports, status_always_zero, status_splits_generated, next_labels, prime_footer; states per task: normal report, empty corpus, env failure
- Verification cadence:
  - Iteration tier: mix test --stale or named files plus mix spec.check --base HEAD; no full suite mid-iteration
  - Final tier: the four common merge-gate commands run-until-green before IMPLEMENTED
  - Verifier tier: tagged tests for the ids above plus --stale only
- Standing bounce-class checks:
  - Production call site named for each new callable surface: agent sessions run spec.prime at session start and spec.next after changes; proving tests are the task output tests
  - Fixture hygiene: reuse L9 fixture projects; nothing compiled
  - Spec surfaces kept fresh for every touched callable/config surface
  - Every conditional clause covered (each state per task; label branches)
- Call-site Integration: production caller is the agent loop (AGENTS.md teaches prime --base HEAD and next); proving tests are the output tests for each state.

Out of Scope (files):
- lib/ancora/gate*, lib/ancora/derive/**, lib/ancora/output* (read-only here)
- lib/ancora/review*, lib/mix/tasks/spec.{review,init,decision.new}.ex
Allowed touches (this stage may modify):
- lib/ancora/prime.ex, lib/ancora/next.ex, lib/ancora/status.ex
- lib/mix/tasks/spec.prime.ex, lib/mix/tasks/spec.next.ex, lib/mix/tasks/spec.status.ex
- test/ancora/{prime,next,status}_test.exs, test/mix/tasks/spec_{prime,next,status}_test.exs, test/support/**
- .spec/specs/ancora.tasks.spec.md (acknowledging edits to requirement/scenario blocks only; never weakening)

Out of Scope (intent):
- no verdict line on any report task; no --json anywhere but spec.check
- no change to spec.next label strings (they are a de facto API)
- no strength summaries, no --bugfix, no --run-commands, no --min-strength

Merge gate:
- [ ] mix compile --warnings-as-errors
- [ ] mix test
- [ ] mix format --check-formatted
- [ ] mix deps.unlock --check-unused
- [ ] mix spec.check --base HEAD emits a verdict line
- [ ] Scope check: diff touches only Allowed globs (mechanical)
- [ ] Auditor APPROVE comment on the ticket

Reasoning:
Both grader FAILs confirmed by direct reading of the stage worktree at f802d8c (base f415c6f).

1. Symmetric fixtures are swap-blind — confirmed. test/ancora/status_test.exs:66-69 asserts project_generated == 1, dep_generated == 1, and "generated=1+1"; the spec scenario ancora.tasks.scenario.status_splits_generated (spec lines 339-347) explicitly demands the asymmetric 1+2 case, which no test demonstrates. lib/ancora/status.ex:155-157 interpolates the two counts adjacently, so a swap there or in subject_rows/4 (status.ex:111-112) is invisible to every assertion; the verifier proved this with a live mutation. Same defect in the empty/thin line: both fixtures yield "empty=1 thin(<3)=1" (status_test.exs:17, spec_status_test.exs:15), and status.ex:146 prints the two counts side by side, so swapping them passes. This violates the standing check "every conditional clause covered" — the derived==0 vs derived<3 branches are never distinguished.

2. Inert callable-surface tests — confirmed. test/mix/tasks/spec_prime_test.exs:41-44, spec_next_test.exs:36-39, spec_status_test.exs:51-54 each do `x = &Mix.Tasks.Spec.X.run/1; assert is_function(x, 1)`. All three carry @tag spec: tags (prime_loop, next_labels_verbatim, report_task_flags), claiming coverage evidence they cannot provide. The real rename protection is the subprocess tests invoking tasks by name.

Grader overlap: both independently caught the generated-split symmetry; the critic adds the empty/thin all-ones case and the inert captures. No disagreement between graders; nothing either found was refuted.

Standard checks:
- Scope: 14 files changed, all inside Allowed globs; spec edits touch only status_derived_report and prime_loop statements and both strengthen (re-verified in the diff).
- Intent: no --json switch on any report task (verified @switches in all three mix tasks); no --bugfix/--run-commands/--min-strength anywhere; no verdict emission (Output.gated whitelist, refuted by tests on every path); labels byte-compared by the verifier against specled_ex.
- Seams: mix tasks are thin delegations to lib modules through Output.gated/2; subprocess runner added in test/support/ancora_case.exs is contained. Clean.
- The exactly_eight deferral to ancora-yzu.29 is honest (verified real by the verifier); no objection.

Bounce reason (itemized, consolidated for the implementer):
1. Make the status fixtures asymmetric in test/ancora/status_test.exs:
   a. "splits project-macro and dependency-generated bindings": one project-macro plus two dep-generated bindings; assert project_generated == 1, dep_generated == 2, and "generated=1+2" — this is the exact case the spec scenario status_splits_generated demands.
   b. "reports empty and thin subjects": add a subject with 1-2 derived bindings so the header reads "derived subjects=2 empty=1 thin(<3)=2", distinguishing the empty and thin counts.
2. Replace the three callable-surface tests (spec_prime_test.exs:41, spec_next_test.exs:36, spec_status_test.exs:51) with real assertions — `Code.ensure_loaded!` + `function_exported?(Mix.Tasks.Spec.X, :run, 1)` or `Mix.Task.get!("spec.x")` — or delete them and move their spec tags onto the subprocess tests that actually pin the task names.

Mechanical-remedy count and classification: 2/2 — both items qualify. Every fix is test-side only, fully prescribed by the graders down to fixture contents and assertion strings, cheap, and touches no production code. No main bounce consumed (0/2 remain). Production behavior appears correct; the defect is that the suite cannot prove it.
